newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila mulls extension of phone roll-out deadline.
newsitem.headline: Manila mulls extension of phone roll-out deadline.

text.p: Philippine Communications Secretary Arturo Enrile said on Thursday he was reviewing the possibility of extending the roll-out programme of new telephone firms for fixed telephone lines beyond the three-year deadline.

Under the law, cellular phone companies are required to install 400,000 telephone fixed lines while new operators of international gateway facilities (IGF) are mandated to put up 300,000 land lines by the end of 1998.
They are required to complete their programmes by year-end or early 1998.
"(The extension) can be done on an administrative basis but this would depend on how reasonable the delays would be," Enrile told reporters.
The National Telecommunications Commission earlier said only a small number of firms were complying with their obligations.
The Philippines has five cellular phone firms and 11 IGF operators.
They include listed firms such as Pilipino Telephone Corp, Globe Telecom, Philippine Telegraph & Telephone Corp and ICC Telecoms, a unit of Benpres Holdings Corp.
